learning_objective: 🎯 Dive into the world of programming by writing your very first Python scripts, understanding variables, and using operators!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language. It is incredibly popular because its syntax is simple, English-like, and easy to learn for beginners.
Python has two modes: Interactive mode (typing code line-by-line and getting instant output) and Script mode (writing a whole program in a file and running it at once).
A variable is like a container in memory used to store data. An identifier is the name given to a variable, function, or class (e.g., `age = 16`, where `age` is the identifier).
Data types define what kind of data a variable holds. Common types in Python are Integers (whole numbers), Floats (decimals), Strings (text), and Booleans (True/False).
Symbols that perform operations on variables and values. Includes Arithmetic (+, -, *, /), Relational/Comparison (==, >, <), and Logical (and, or, not).

fun_activity.title: 🗣️ Talk to Python
fun_activity.instructions: Open the Python interactive shell (IDLE). Type `print("Hello, World!")` and press Enter. Then type `5 * 8` and press Enter. You are now officially talking to a computer in Python!

exam_tips: 📌 Remember the rules for naming identifiers: they cannot start with a number and cannot be a Python keyword.
📌 Distinguish between `/` (normal division, returns float) and `//` (floor division, returns integer).
📌 The `=` symbol is the assignment operator (assigns a value), while `==` is the equality operator (checks if two values are equal).
quick_recap: ⭐ Python is an interpreted language, meaning it executes code line by line.
⭐ Comments in Python start with the `#` symbol and are ignored by the interpreter.
⭐ You can use the `type()` function to find out the data type of any variable.
